a.p: This website tells the stories of equipment that NASA missions left behind on the Moon and Mars, from rovers and landers to a helicopter. It is written for beginners who want to see what was sent, what it discovered and what became of it.
When a space mission ends, much of its hardware stays where it worked. For example:

ul: The Apollo Lunar Module descent stages were left at each of the six Apollo lunar landing sites.
Surveyor 3 remains on the lunar surface. Apollo 12 astronauts brought back only selected parts of it.
Spirit and Opportunity have both ended their missions on Mars.
Ingenuity remains on Mars and can no longer fly.

a.p: Only NASA missions. Equipment from other organisations or countries is outside the scope of this website.

faqs.q: What have Moon and Mars equipment discovered?

a.p: A few highlights from the featured equipment:

ul: Surveyor 3's surface-sampling tests helped scientists conclude that the Moon's surface could support an Apollo Lunar Module.
The Lunar Roving Vehicle extended how far Apollo astronauts could explore on the surface.
Spirit found strong evidence that Mars was once much wetter than it is today.
Opportunity found evidence that Mars may once have been able to sustain microbial life.
Ingenuity made the first powered, controlled flight on another planet.

a.p: Use the menu at the top of every page to reach destinations, library tools and information about the website.

ul: Open search with the search button, or press the slash key or Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on a Mac).
Search starts after you type two characters.

faqs.q: What are the maps and timelines?

a.p: Maps are meant to show where equipment is located, and timelines to show when missions took place. These sections are still being built.
Compare is meant to let you view pieces of equipment side by side. This section is still being built.

faqs.q: What are the Quiz and eLearning sections?

a.p: The Quiz is meant to help you test what you have learned, and eLearning to offer guided learning about exploration equipment. Both sections are still being built.
